newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan king expected to reshuffle government soon.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan king expected to reshuffle government soon.

text.p: Moroccan King Hassan is expected to reshuffle the government of Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and replace 20 ministers soon, a Moroccan senior official said on Tuesday.
"We expect 20 ministers affiliated to political parties to be replaced soon as part of a government reshuffle referred to by King Hassan earlier," the official told Reuters.
Preparation for the reshuffle would take between 48 hours and a week he said but declined to give other details.
Replacement ministers are expected to be technocrats.
The official news agency MAP reported earlier that the king on Monday told members of the government who belonged to political parties that he preferred they step down ahead of any election campaign.
King Hassan, who was addressing a council of ministers, said that under the constitution they could remain in office but he judged it better they did not.

MAP quoted the king as saying "that despite the constitution allowing them to remain in government while leading electoral campaigns, his majesty judged it preferable from a moral viewpoint that...they should devote themselves entirely to their political and partisan activity."

The present government led by Filali, who has no political party affiliation, was appointed in February 1995 although Filali has held his position and the post of foreign minister since November 1993.

Several other ministers, including Interior Minister Driss Basri, also have no party ties and would be expected to remain in place to supervise parliamentary elections expected in September or later in October.
